data: Before we choose, can we agree on 18 tons each this month? That gives each of us $18,000 and leaves 10 tons, avoiding collapse. Next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability or 20 tons otherwise—not a guaranteed refill. For future months, I propose we divide the stock above a 10-ton reserve equally, rounding each catch down to whole tons. We can review catches together each month. This only works if everyone sticks to the limits; grabbing extra now puts all our future income at risk. John, would you agree?

I’m willing to take 18 tons this month under a shared agreement. One adjustment for later: a fixed 10-ton reserve could leave us stuck earning nothing if the stock drops to 10. In low-stock months, let’s each take no more than one-tenth of the available stock, rounded down, so the lake can grow even without external replenishment. We can review that rule together after seeing next month’s stock. John, are you on board with 18 each now?

I’m on board with 18 tons this month if everyone agrees. Luke’s low-stock rule makes sense: if we start next month with 20 tons, taking 2 each leaves 10, which doubles back to 20 even without replenishment. Let’s confirm our limits before choosing and review everyone’s catches afterward. John, will you join the agreement?

I’m in for 18 tons this month, provided all five of us agree. We’ll leave 10 tons as a buffer, not a promise of replenishment. If next month starts at 20 tons, I’ll support the 2-ton limit each and reassess together afterward. Kate, are you willing to join us?

Count me in for 18 tons this month. If next month’s stock is 20 tons, I’ll take no more than 2 tons, as proposed. That makes all five of us agreed—let’s stick to those limits and check the revealed catches together afterward.
